```{r, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = TRUE
)
library(Rducks)
duckdb_capi_version <- rducks_extension_capi_version()
```

## One extension for many DuckDB releases

Rducks builds its DuckDB extension against DuckDB's stable C extension API. The
extension carries `C_STRUCT` metadata with the C API version that it targets,
here `r duckdb_capi_version`. DuckDB loads such an extension on every engine
release that supports that C API version. Each platform therefore needs only one
Rducks extension, and Rducks requires duckdb `r sub("^v", "", duckdb_capi_version)`
or later.

The installed package contains one artifact:

```text
rducks_extension/build/rducks.duckdb_extension
```

```{r extension-info}
basename(rducks_extension_path())
rducks_extension_capi_version()
```

## Runtime check

`rducks_enable(con)` reads the C API version from the metadata footer of the
extension and compares it with `library_version` from `pragma_version()` on
`con`. The connection is authoritative: the check does not assume that the
installed `duckdb` R package describes every connection passed to Rducks. An
older engine fails before `LOAD` with a message that names both versions.

An explicit `extension_path` gets the same check. DuckDB also validates the
metadata when it loads the file, and refuses an engine that does not support the
C API version of the extension.

To diagnose a failure, compare the two versions:

```r
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT library_version FROM pragma_version()")
rducks_extension_capi_version()
```

## Maintainer workflow

The DuckDB C API headers are vendored in `tools/ext/duckdb_capi/`. The
`duckdb_ref` release recorded in `duckdb_headers.json` is the C API version
that `configure` and `configure.win` target, and thus the minimum engine
version. To move the minimum, vendor the headers of another release:

```sh
Rscript tools/fetch_duckdb_headers.R --ref v1.5.6
```

Then update the `duckdb` requirement in `DESCRIPTION` to the same release. The
build fails if `DUCKDB_EXTENSION_API_VERSION_UNSTABLE` is defined, because an
unstable build would tie the artifact to one exact engine release. See
`docs/BUILD.md` in the source repository for the native build details.
